name: Saint Peter Canisius
history: The first Dutch Jesuit, who spent fifty years renewing the Catholic faith in Germany, Austria and Switzerland after the upheaval of the Reformation. He founded colleges, preached tirelessly and wrote catechisms that went through hundreds of editions. He is called the second apostle of Germany and was named a Doctor of the Church in 1925.
life: Peter Kanis was born at Nijmegen and studied at Cologne. In 1543 he made the Spiritual Exercises under Saint Peter Faber at Mainz and entered the young Society of Jesus. He attended the Council of Trent as a theologian, taught at Ingolstadt and Vienna, and became the first provincial of the Jesuits in Upper Germany. He founded or helped found colleges at Prague, Munich, Innsbruck and elsewhere, preached constantly and refused the archbishopric of Vienna. His catechisms, beginning in 1555, were so widely used that in some German lands a catechism was simply called a ‘Canisius’. He urged that those who had left the Church be treated with patience and charity, and he relied more on teaching and example than on argument. His last years were spent at Fribourg in Switzerland, where he founded the college of Saint Michael and died in 1597.
prayerTo: Saint Peter Canisius, you rebuilt the Church in your time by patient teaching and tireless love. Pray for catechists, priests and teachers, and for all who have drifted from the faith. Give me a clear knowledge of what the Church believes, and the charity to share it gently. Amen.
penance: Learn one answer from the Catechism by heart today. Pray for someone who has left the Church, and treat them with special kindness.
meditation: He spent fifty years teaching the faith to children and simple people, one question and answer at a time. Could you explain your faith simply if a child asked you?
prayer: O God, who didst give strength and learning to blessed Peter thy Confessor for the defense of the Catholic faith, mercifully grant, that by his example and teaching the erring may be saved and the faithful remain constant in the confession of truth. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
